lines.native: ¡Hola! ¿Tienes tiempo? Just five more minutes. Tengo una pregunta—ooh, ¿qué es eso? This is so random.
lines.translation: Hello! Do you have time? Just five more minutes. I have a question—ooh, what is that? This is so random.
lines.narrative: The cracked fountain drips with municipal uncertainty. Flick appears at the edge of your vision; looking directly at him proves unhelpful. A tiny firecracker pops.

lines.native: ¿Dónde? ¿Qué es? You told me to look, not stop moving. Attention span: excellent, unfortunately misdirected. ¿Otra pregunta? Tengo tiempo. Well, five more minutes. Can you make me stop—in Spanish?
lines.translation: Where? What is it? You told me to look, not stop moving. Attention span: excellent, unfortunately misdirected. Another question? I have time. Well, five more minutes. Can you make me stop—in Spanish?
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains in the corner of your vision, where accountability has trouble focusing.

lines.native: ¡Vale, vale! No me muevo. You stopped me. Attention span: rude but effective. ¿A la izquierda o a la derecha? Which way? Pick a direction for me—actually, first, a riddle: what has two feet and five more minutes?
lines.translation: Okay, okay! I’m not moving. You stopped me. Attention span: rude but effective. To the left or to the right? Which way? Pick a direction for me—actually, first, a riddle: what has two feet and five more minutes?
lines.narrative: Flick stops at the edge of your vision. A tiny firecracker continues forward, apparently exempt from the instruction.

lines.native: ¿Left? Eso es inglés. Necesito una dirección en español. ¿Dónde voy? Your attention span gets a seven. Translation pending. Tengo una adivinanza—oh, mira, una hoja.
lines.translation: Left? That's English. I need a direction in Spanish. Where do I go? Your attention span gets a seven. Translation pending. I have a riddle—oh, look, a leaf.
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops at your elbow. Flick is elsewhere, by the strict definition of wherever you look.

lines.native: ¡Sí, a la izquierda! Muy bien. Pero ahora no. Mañana, ¿vale? Tengo una adivinanza—actually, just one more. Five more minutes. ¿Podemos esperar?
lines.translation: Yes, to the left! Very good. But not now. Tomorrow, okay? I have a riddle—actually, just one more. Five more minutes. Can we wait?
lines.narrative: Flick darts left, just beyond your gaze. A tiny firecracker pops beside a sign reading TEMPORARILY TOMORROW.

lines.native: ¡Mañana, perfecto! Hoy no. Tenemos tiempo. You agreed to tomorrow—procrastination gets a gold star. ¿Podemos esperar un poco más? Tengo una adivinanza… ooh, una mosca.
lines.translation: Tomorrow, perfect! Not today. We have time. You agreed to tomorrow—procrastination gets a gold star. Can we wait a little longer? I have a riddle… ooh, a fly.
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains at the edge of your vision, where responsibility has poor reception.

lines.native: ¡Ahora! Sí, ahora. No mañana. Voy a la izquierda. You win. Attention span: ten out of ten, deeply inconvenient. ¿Qué tiene dos pies y—? Fine. Moving now. Qué raro.
lines.translation: Now! Yes, now. Not tomorrow. I’m going left. You win. Attention span: ten out of ten, deeply inconvenient. What has two feet and—? Fine. Moving now. How strange.
lines.narrative: Flick’s tiny firecracker goes off behind you. For once, it sounds less like a distraction and more like a resignation. Something at the edge of your vision shuffles left.
